question: persister
prompt:
Research question: "What measurements or analyses would best reveal why a small fraction of genetically identical cancer cells survive targeted drug treatment?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Barcoded lineage tracing across drug pulses
ideas.description: Introduce heritable cellular barcodes (e.g., CellTag or lentiviral barcode libraries) into a clonal population, then apply the targeted drug and track which barcoded lineages survive. Comparing barcode frequencies before and after treatment, and across washout and re-challenge, shows whether survivors were pre-existing rare clones or arose through drug-induced reprogramming.

ideas.title: Pre-treatment sorting and profiling of future survivors
ideas.description: Use live-cell reporters or surface markers to sort cells before drug exposure, then profile sorted subpopulations and the survivor fraction with single-cell RNA-seq and ATAC-seq. This tests whether a transcriptional or chromatin state that predicts survival already exists in the untreated population.

ideas.title: Live-cell signaling and cell-cycle reporters linked to fate
ideas.description: Express biosensors such as ERK or AKT kinase translocation reporters and FUCCI cell-cycle markers, then image individual cells continuously through drug addition and record their fate. Correlating signaling amplitude, dynamics, and cell-cycle phase at the moment of treatment with eventual survival identifies the dynamic states that predict persistence.

ideas.title: Genome-wide and single-cell CRISPR screens under drug pressure
ideas.description: Run pooled CRISPR knockout or CRISPRi screens with the drug, comparing guide representation in surviving versus dying cells, and follow hits with Perturb-seq to see how each perturbation shifts the persister state. Hits from chromatin, signaling, and stress-response genes point to the mechanisms that enable survival, and validation of top candidates tests whether they are necessary and sufficient.

ideas.title: Metabolic and epigenetic priming profiling with washout and re-challenge
ideas.description: Measure metabolic state (for example NAD(P)H fluorescence lifetime imaging, mitochondrial respiration, and metabolomics) and key histone marks or chromatin accessibility in pre-treatment, early-treatment, and surviving cells. Then remove the drug and re-challenge: if survivors retain their metabolic or epigenetic signature across several passages, the data point to a heritable adaptive memory, while loss of the signature implies a reversible tolerance state.
